# The data-stage acceptance golden, one line per engine:
#
#     <engine>  <sha256 of `jq -S .` over data-raw-dump.json> <sha256 of `jq -S .` over mod-settings-dump.json>  <the mod set>
#
# Written and checked by scripts/run-datastage.sh, which packages
# guest/{go,rust}/examples/datastage as a mod, runs `factorio --dump-data`, and
# hashes both normalised dumps.
#
# WHY TWO HASHES. Setting prototypes live in the settings stage's own Lua state
# and never reach data-raw-dump.json, so a golden over the data dump alone is
# green for a guest whose fk_settings hook silently did nothing. The settings
# dump is where they land, and hashing it is what lets the settings stage fail.
#
# WHY NORMALISED. Key order in the dumps is INSERTION order, so two mods
# differing only in the order they call data:extend produce dumps that differ at
# a byte and describe the same game. `jq -S` sorts every object; measured, that
# removes an ordering difference completely and preserves a real field-value
# change.
#
# WHY THE MOD SET IS HERE. The dump is a function of every mod that ran, and
# Factorio's bundled DLC data loads whatever --mod-directory says -- so a
# machine that owns different DLC produces a different dump for a mod that is
# perfectly fine. Recorded so a mismatch names its own cause and reads as SKIP
# rather than as a broken mod.
#
# WHY PER ENGINE. base's own prototypes move between series, so a hash taken on
# one engine says nothing about another. A line is re-taken on its own engine
# whenever the example guests change; the 2026-08-30 change (the settings->data
# round trip, plus the env(4)/env(5) log lines) invalidated every earlier line
# at once, so this file was re-taken from scratch on the engine then installed.
# An engine with no line reads as "record it" rather than as a failure; switch
# the Steam branch and run the script to add one.
